prompt: Was the founder of the bank that was established 42 years before the National Banking Act was expanded to include the Territory of Hawai'i still alive when it acquired Pioneer Federal Savings Bank?
answer: No. The bank was **Bishop & Co., founded in 1858**—42 years before federal national-banking legislation was extended to the Territory of Hawaiʻi in 1900. Its founders were **Charles Reed Bishop and William A. Aldrich**. Bishop died in **1915** (and Aldrich also died long before 1993), whereas First Hawaiian completed its acquisition of Pioneer Federal Savings Bank in **August 1993**. Thus, the founder was not alive at the time of the acquisition.
